title: A map of coherent modules injective, surjective or bijective on one stalk is so on a neighbourhood
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ a homomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $x\in X$, with stalks and stalk maps $\varphi_x:\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal F_x$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; for an open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal F|_U$ is the restriction ($\mathcal F|_U(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ open). (1) If $\mathcal F_x=0$, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ with $\mathcal F|_U=0$. (2) If $\varphi_x$ is injective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is injective (on the sections over every open $V\subseteq U$). (3) If $\varphi_x$ is surjective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is surjective (as a map of sheaves). (4) If $\varphi_x$ is bijective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U:\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y3 (label lemma-local-isomorphism); its proof cites Modules, Lemmas finite-type-surjective-on-stalk, finite-type-stalk-zero and finite-type-to-coherent-injective-on-stalk

proof.text: Conventions. Coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules are in particular of finite type ([pqf-def-coherent] (3) requires (2)), and finite type in [pqf-def-coherent] (2) (locally a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$) is finite type in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1) on the ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The kernel $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $V\mapsto\ker(\varphi_V)$ of $\mathcal G$; so $\varphi|_U$ is injective on the sections over every open $V\subseteq U$ iff $\mathcal K|_U=0$. The locally Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is not used: the proof below works on any scheme (indeed any ringed space) with coherent in the sense of [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y3 (label lemma-local-isomorphism, line 2364) and its proof

proof.text: Part (3). $\mathcal F$ is of finite type (step 1) and $\varphi_x$ is surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk] gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B8 (lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk, line 876), cited by the proof of 01Y3

proof.text: Claim (Modules 01B9): if $\mathcal H$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type with $\mathcal H_x=0$, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ with $\mathcal H|_U=0$. Proof: apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk] to the zero map $0\to\mathcal H$; its stalk map $0\to\mathcal H_x=0$ is surjective. This gives $U\ni x$ open such that for every open $W\subseteq U$ and $t\in\mathcal H(W)$ there is an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ with $t|_{W_i}$ in the image of $0$, i.e. $t|_{W_i}=0$ for all $i$; since $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $t=0$. So $\mathcal H(W)=0$ for every open $W\subseteq U$, i.e. $\mathcal H|_U=0$. Part (1) is the claim for $\mathcal H=\mathcal F$, which is of finite type by step 1.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B9 (lemma-finite-type-stalk-zero, line 897) and its proof (special case of 01B8 for 0 -> F), cited by the proof of 01Y3

proof.text: Part (2) (Modules 01C0). Let $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi\subseteq\mathcal G$. Since $\mathcal G$ is of finite type (step 1) and $\mathcal F$ is coherent, $\mathcal K$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-finite-type-sub-kernel] (2). Next $\mathcal K_x=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: an element of $\mathcal K_x$ is a germ $k_x$ of some $k\in\mathcal K(V)$, $x\in V$ open, so $k\in\mathcal G(V)$ with $\varphi_V(k)=0$; then $\varphi_x$ sends the germ of $k$ in $\mathcal G_x$ to $(\varphi_V(k))_x=0$, so by injectivity of $\varphi_x$ the germ of $k$ in $\mathcal G_x$ is $0$, i.e. $k|_W=0$ in $\mathcal G(W)$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq V$; as $\mathcal K(W)\subseteq\mathcal G(W)$ with the restriction of $\mathcal G$, $k|_W=0$ in $\mathcal K(W)$ and $k_x=0$ in $\mathcal K_x$. By the claim of step 3 applied to $\mathcal H=\mathcal K$ there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ with $\mathcal K|_U=0$, i.e. $\varphi_V$ is injective for every open $V\subseteq U$ (step 1).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01C0 (lemma-finite-type-to-coherent-injective-on-stalk, line 1781) and its proof (K = Ker(phi) is of finite type by Lemma 01BY, K_x = 0, then Lemma 01B9), cited by the proof of 01Y3

proof.text: Part (4). If $\varphi_x$ is bijective, steps 4 and 2 give open neighbourhoods $U_1,U_2$ of $x$ with $\varphi|_{U_1}$ injective on sections and $\varphi|_{U_2}$ surjective as a map of sheaves; put $U=U_1\cap U_2$. For an open $V\subseteq U$, $\varphi_V$ is injective; it is also surjective: given $t\in\mathcal F(V)$ choose an open covering $V=\bigcup_iV_i$ and $g_i\in\mathcal G(V_i)$ with $\varphi_{V_i}(g_i)=t|_{V_i}$; on $V_i\cap V_j$ both $g_i|$ and $g_j|$ map to $t|_{V_i\cap V_j}$, so they agree by injectivity of $\varphi_{V_i\cap V_j}$; by the sheaf property of $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] they glue to $g\in\mathcal G(V)$, and $\varphi_V(g)$ and $t$ agree on every $V_i$, hence are equal. So each $\varphi_V$ ($V\subseteq U$) is a bijective $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear map; the inverses $\psi_V=\varphi_V^{-1}$ are $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear and commute with restrictions (apply the injective $\varphi_{V'}$ to $\psi_V(t)|_{V'}$ and to $\psi_{V'}(t|_{V'})$), so $\psi:\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules inverse to $\varphi|_U$, and $\varphi|_U$ is an isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_local_isomorphism (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : SheafOfModules (moduleRings X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace F) (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace G) (φ : G ⟶ F) (x : X) : (IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj F) → ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsZero (F.over U)) ∧ (Function.Injective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map φ) → ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ (V : X.Opens), V ≤ U → Function.Injective (ConcreteCategory.hom (φ.val.app (.op V)))) ∧ (Function.Surjective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map φ) → ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Epi ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace) U).map φ)) ∧ (Function.Bijective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map φ) → ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace) U).map φ))
